title: structured-output: integrate CFG-backed constrained decoder with tokenizer-aware regex fallbacks
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary: This PR adds a CFG-backed constrained decoding backend and a tokenizer-aware regex fallback layer for structured-output constraints. Motivation: existing regex-only constrained decoding fails on tokenizer edge cases (multi-token punctuation, unicode splits) and CFG constraints perform better for hierarchical outputs, but we need robust fallbacks for user-provided regexes and OpenAI-compat tooling. This change unifies both approaches with a routing layer that selects CFG decoding when a grammar is provided and falls back to tokenizer-aware regex constraints when a grammar is absent or when the CFG fails to cover an observed tokenization split. It also includes several hardening fixes to the OpenAI compatibility layer so function/tool-calling plus structured output work stably over streaming responses.

What changed (high level):
- Added a new constrained decoder implementation: src/decoders/constrained_cfg_decoder.rs (Rust) and a thin shim in src/decoders/mod.rs to select backend.
- Implemented tokenizer-aware regex fallback heuristics in src/decoders/regex_fallback.rs which pre-tokenizes candidate regex fragments using the active tokenizer and adds allowed token sequences for common split patterns (emoji, multi-byte punctuation, whitespace variants).
- Updated OpenAI-compat layer to expose structured-output constraint metadata across streaming chunks: src/openai_compat/streaming_constraints.rs. This fixes edgecases where regex spans were split across streamed deltas.
- Added comprehensive unit and integration tests: tests/structured_output/tokenizer_edgecases.rs, tests/openai_compat/streaming_structured_output.rs, and a new fuzz harness tests/fuzz/tokenizer_regex_harness.rs.
- Added docs and usage examples: docs/structured-output.md and examples/structured-output/cfg-example.py.
- Small changes to Python and TS SDK wrappers to surface structured constraint errors: sdks/python/redwood/structured_output.py and sdks/typescript/src/structuredOutput.ts.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add CFG decoder implementation + routing
- [x] Implement tokenizer-aware regex fallback
- [x] Fix OpenAI streaming constraint propagation
- [x] Add unit/integration/fuzz tests
- [x] Update SDK wrappers and docs
- [x] Run perf benchmarks and ensure no regression on 2048 seq throughput (micro-bench results in CI)

Commits (summary):
- "Add cfg-backed constrained decoder and routing layer"
- "Tokenizer-aware regex fallback heuristics and utilities"
- "Fix: propagate constraint spans in streaming deltas (OpenAI compat)"
- "tests: tokenizer edgecases + streaming structured-output tests"
- "docs: structured-output guide and examples"

Files changed (high level):
- src/decoders/constrained_cfg_decoder.rs (+280 LOC)
- src/decoders/regex_fallback.rs (+190 LOC)
- src/openai_compat/streaming_constraints.rs (+60 LOC)
- src/decoders/mod.rs (router changes)
- tests/structured_output/tokenizer_edgecases.rs
- tests/openai_compat/streaming_structured_output.rs
- tests/fuzz/tokenizer_regex_harness.rs
- docs/structured-output.md
- examples/structured-output/cfg-example.py
- sdks/python/redwood/structured_output.py
- sdks/typescript/src/structuredOutput.ts

Testing and CI:
- Initial CI run showed a failure in the tokenizer fuzz harness due to an assumption about NFKC normalization. I pushed a follow-up commit to normalize inputs before tokenization and re-ran CI. Final CI results: all unit tests passing, integration tests passing, lint fixed, and benchmark micro-tail latency within 3% of baseline for 2048 sequence workloads. CI checks included build, unit, integration, fuzz, lint, and perf checks.

Review notes and design rationale:
- CFG vs regex: CFGs provide stronger structural guarantees and are preferred for nested or hierarchical outputs (e.g., JSON with nested objects). However, many users provide quick regex constraints; rather than rejecting them when tokenization breaks spans, this PR implements a tokenizer-aware fallback that generates token-level accept sets derived from regex matches and common multi-token splits.
- Routing: the decoder router favors CFG when a grammar is supplied. If CFG fails to accept any candidate tokens for a prefix (rare), we attempt the regex fallback as a secondary path to avoid dead-ends. This keeps customer workloads resilient in the presence of imperfect constraints.
- OpenAI streaming fixes: streaming deltas no longer lose constraint context across chunks; we attach a stable constraint frame id to each stream and use it in the server-side decoder to maintain state. This change required minimal SDK surface updates.

Backports and release notes: backport candidate for release/2026-02-1 (recommended) because this fixes several customer-facing tokenizer regressions. See release_notes field.

Migration / rollout: This is backwards-compatible for existing clients. CFG support is opt-in (users must supply a grammar). Regex fallback is enabled by default for regex constraints but can be toggled by the decoder config.

If you want to exercise the new behavior locally: see examples/structured-output/cfg-example.py and run the new fuzz harness with `cargo test --test tokenizer_edgecases` or `python -m pytest tests/structured_output`.

Acknowledgements: thanks to Noah for the CFG design review and Mateo for the tokenizer heuristics and fuzz harness.

review_thread: Noah Chen: The CFG implementation looks solid; two nits on error messages and an edgecase where the CFG could accept an ambiguous production. Please add a comment and a test.
Priya Kapoor: Thanks Noah — added comment and a regression test (tests/structured_output/ambiguous_cfg_case.rs) in the follow-up commit.

Mateo Alvarez: Fuzzer found a tokenization normalization issue on first run. Suggested normalizing input with NFKC.
Priya Kapoor: Implemented NFKC normalization and added tests to the fuzz harness.

Sara Thompson: Can you add a short cookbook entry to docs describing when to use CFG vs regex?
Priya Kapoor: Added a cookbook section and example in docs/structured-output.md.
Noah Chen: Approve after the small doc tweak was applied.

release_notes: Bugfix/feature: Add CFG-backed constrained decoding with tokenizer-aware regex fallbacks to improve structured-output stability for tokenizer edge cases. Streaming constraint propagation fixed for OpenAI compatibility. Backport recommended for 2026-02-1.
notes: No user-facing API changes required; SDK surfaces updated to return structured constraint errors consistently.
